messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: sev2 detected — recurring CUDA OOM + container crash pattern on serving-pool-usw2 (paged-attn allocator). Auto-escalation to oncall.
maria: Seeing a slow, steady increase in resident GPU memory on nodes running the paged-attn allocator. Not instantaneous, more like a 24–48h creep until OOM/restart. Pattern: KV cache fragmentation + small spills -> allocator can't reclaim.
ashok: +1. Logs show repeated page faults and `cudaFree` failures before the crash. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15 02:12:38] ERROR runtime: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
[...]
allocator: failed to evict page (id=0x7f9c2) attempt=3
KVCache: resident_bytes=12434567890 free_fragments=2
```
lee: Customer impact: A subset of long-context (>=6k token) requests started returning 503s and timeouts this morning. CS (jamie-cs) says 4 customers reported increased errors, one started using fallback model.
jamie-cs: Notified the customers we have a mitigation plan. They want ETA for sustained fix; we offered short window workaround (disable long sequences / route to dedicated pool). Customers ok for now but want updates.
devops-bot: Auto-restarts observed. Pod restart counts increased from 0->4 in last hour on nodes gpu-12,gpu-14.
sre-liz: Immediate mitigations we should try in this thread (quick wins):
- temporarily reduce `MAX_SEQUENCE_LEN` for hosted model route to 4096
- increase KV eviction aggressiveness (env `KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.6`)
- cordon + drain most affected nodes and move workloads to spare pool
- enable more aggressive prefix/KV caching TTLs
maria: I'm going to apply the env tweak on the canary deployment, then scale up spare capacity. Patching config now:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/hosted-model-serving KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.6
kubectl -n inference patch deployment/hosted-model-serving -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"MAX_SEQUENCE_LEN","value":"4096"}]}]}}}}'
```
ashok: Also adding a hotfix to allocator to avoid stale slab retention — small change to free-list traversal we can hotpatch, PR: runtime#5921. If we roll that we should do canary and watch for memory regression.
runtime-ron: I'm +1 on the hotpatch but we need to avoid noisy restarts. Plan: 1) patch canary image with allocator change; 2) run canary with `KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.6` & `MAX_SEQUENCE_LEN=4096`; 3) monitor resident_bytes and eviction_hits/eviction_misses.
lee: I'm updating the incident ticket and customer notes. Linking the alert graph here: https://internal.metrics/graphs/serving-pool-usw2?range=6h
maria: Canary applied to pool-canary-3. Early signs: resident_bytes growth rate down ~45% over 20m. No OOMs yet. Will let it run 1h.
sre-liz: If canary holds, plan to roll to remaining nodes with staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and keep MAX_SEQUENCE_LEN cap until allocator fix ships. Also add a short-term k8s liveness policy change to avoid thundering restarts: extend crash backoff.
ashok: Noted an edge case: aggressive eviction reduces quality slightly for some prompts (prefix KV gone). We should coordinate with runtime/evals to track regeneration rate.
jamie-cs: Customers updated: they accept temporary reductions in max length. One asked about SLA impact — minimal so far.
devops-bot: Performed `kubectl cordon gpu-12,gpu-14` and created replacement nodes in spare pool.
maria: Rolling to 30% now. Will post metrics in 10m. Also enabling extra debug traces for eviction (short lived): `EVICT_DEBUG=1`.
runtime-ron: Can we capture allocator heap snapshots before and after rollout to compare fragmentation patterns? If yes, please upload to the incident ticket.
ashok: Captured heapdumps at t0 (before patch) and t1 (10m after canary). Attaching to ticket: s3://incidents/4765432100/heapdump-t0, heapdump-t1.
lee: Timeline update in ticket. Adding action items: (1) short-term: aggressive eviction + max_seq cap + staged rollout (done/ongoing), (2) medium-term: allocator hotpatch PR#5921 (code change), canary then broad rollout, (3) long-term: refactor allocator slab compaction and KV compaction strategy w/ evict-on-slab-scan.
maria: Observation: nodes that had repeated paged-attn bursts (long multi-turn chats) show the worst fragmentation. Recommend throttling long user sessions if we see repeated OOMs during rollout.
sre-liz: Postmortem owner: runtime-ron. Expected postmortem ETA: 72h after incident stabilization. Add follow-ups for customer communication.
runtime-ron: Acknowledged. Will drive the postmortem and allocator deeper investigation. Next steps: ship hotpatch to stable in staged manner once canary stable for 2 hours.
jamie-cs: I'll send formal status email to impacted customers after stabilization.
lee: handing off to night oncall with summary: canary stable (30% -> holding), mitigations active (KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.6, MAX_SEQUENCE_LEN=4096), hotpatch PR opened (runtime#5921). Monitoring alarms adjusted. If node flaps continue, escalate to infra and consider temporary capacity reservation for affected customers. @night-oncall please ack and continue observation. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: HANDOFF: incident thread handed to night-oncall at 4765435800. Marking this thread for follow-up.
